title: Start with one useful promise
intro: Choose where you are starting, then describe the first useful result. You can leave anything uncertain for the conversation.

items.why: Your starting point determines whether we explore an idea, preview setup, or inspect an existing workflow.
items.ifNoAnswer: We can work it out in conversation.

options.label: An idea before code
options.because: You want to decide what should work before building.
options.then: Explore one user job and a concrete success example.

options.label: A new project
options.because: You want to choose a first workflow and the setup it needs.
options.then: Preview the smallest setup and draft the selected outcome.

options.label: An established product
options.because: There is existing behaviour to understand and improve.
options.then: Choose one feature to inspect, using user impact and recurring problems.

options.label: Already using Promise
options.because: Existing outcomes and evidence may already cover this job.
options.then: Find the current capability and preview the smallest useful change.

items.text: Who needs to do what first, and why does it matter now?
items.why: This gives the first promise a useful boundary and keeps the discussion focused.
items.ifNoAnswer: We will explore a couple of possible workflows before choosing.
items.example: A head of year reviews a batch of teacher reports so that corrections reach the right teacher.

items.text: What is one concrete example that would show this worked?
items.why: A visible result helps decide what evidence the first promise needs.
items.blocks: Choosing how to check the outcome.
items.ifNoAnswer: The success check stays open while we refine the workflow.
items.example: Given two teachers' reports, each teacher receives only the feedback intended for them.
